hypothesis: NeuroAI can supply testable mechanisms, but biological analogy should only enter MeshyAnts when converted into a falsifiable software experiment.
falsification_condition: An adopted idea has no measurable prediction, treats a podcast as evidence, or is already implied by a simpler scheduler with no leftover test.

scientific_skeptic.strongest_objection: A2/A4/A3 are software patterns with a DOI attached; verification is URL liveness, not claim binding.

scheduler_critic.strongest_objection: A1–A7 are expressible as labeled queue, router, DAG, manager, or Brooks subsumption. No leftover primitive.

performance_critic.note: No runtime system was claimed. Watch cost is one literature pass plus HTTP checks.

failure_critic.note: No leases, workers, or external effects in this slice.

slop_evaluator.strongest_objection: verification.json PASS is schema+HTTP; S9/S10a/S8b authors were wrong.

baseline_results.outcome: Critic judges all adopted ideas already expressible by those systems. Flat blackboard is a handicapped baseline.

cost_latency_model_calls.note: S5 and S9 returned 403 and were counted ok. That check is not a paper-read.

strongest_objection: NeuroAI did not name a coordination primitive a simpler scheduler cannot already express. Author errors (S9 Karakoc; S10a Karalis; S8b Amazon Science) show the source ledger was not bound to Crossref/arXiv metadata.
next_action: Demote A2–A5 from adopted NeuroAI mechanisms to software priors; keep A1 vs subsumption as the only leftover empirical question; treat A6/A7 as experiment-design constraints; fix authors; replace URL-ok with Crossref/arXiv claim binding.
target_challenge: MESH-107 success_criteria (name a prediction) are too cheap. The load-bearing bar is leftover isolation vs simpler schedulers.
